newsitem.title: UK: Former Barings boss fights to get bonus payment.
newsitem.headline: Former Barings boss fights to get bonus payment.

text.p: Questions over responsibility for the collapse of Barings will resurface next week when Mary Walz, former equity derivatives head at its investment banking arm, begins a claim for 500,000 pounds ($785,000) in unpaid bonuses.
The preliminary hearing, at the Stratford industrial tribunal in east London, will decide if the claim can go ahead.

Walz was among those dismissed by Dutch financial services company Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING) when it took over the blue-blooded bank, which collapsed following huge losses run up by Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson.
A spokeswoman for ING Barings, the London-based investment banking arm of ING, told Reuters the claim would be contested.
"ING Barings will be there and we will be contesting the action," she said.

An official at the industrial tribunals service, which is run by Britain's Department of Trade and Industry, said the hearing was a "Wages Act claim" and would be held on Monday, but could give no further details.

Barings was brought down in February 1995 by Leeson's unauthorised derivatives trading losses of nearly $1.4 billion. ING stepped in and bought the bank, paying bonuses to those who it retained. ($1=.6350 Pound)
